items.text: The Story of Tomorrow
Joint Committee of SF

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Sorry, I didn't ... What did you say?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: It's okay. I'll repeat it for you. Please pay attention this time.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Laplace updated our diagnosis of Ms. Isolde's condition while you were receiving treatment.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: We've determined that she's experiencing a state similar to post-traumatic stress disorder, one that is particularly persistent.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: To put it simply, she's gone crazy.
Kakania unconsciously clenches her fist. It seems to have become her habit.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Then her condition, it isn't because of my hypnosis?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: No.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Even taking into account the unknown of your arcane skill, hypnosis couldn't achieve such a large shift in personality.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: As it turns out, she was actually unable to cooperate with us, not unwilling to.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: We're sorry, Ms. Klara. I understand you accepted the treatment in order to better control your arcane skill because of her.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: But given her current condition, we strongly suggest you don't use your arcane skill on her, as it could stimulate her already unstable state.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: May I at least take a look at her?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I've read through the visitation rules. I promise I won't make physical contact, nor will I pass her the mirror in case I cast my arcane skill.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: That still poses considerable risk.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: She seems to think she's still an opera singer living in Vienna. Before those family tragedies ever happened.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: The Foundation staff guarding her are strangers, so they won't trigger her memories.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: But you, you're different, Ms. Klara.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Your arcane skill, or even just your presence, might trigger her memories. Considering Ms. Isolde's arcane skill and the potential damage it might cause, triggering it will only raise her threat level, and we'll be forced to reduce the already limited freedom she has.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: We're trying our best to avoid that.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Personally, I'd suggest against ...

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: breaking this fragile balance we've managed to maintain.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Not even a single meeting? I just want to see her.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Maybe just once, as long as you promise not to try to dehypnotize her.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I promise!

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: Then I'll submit a visitation request for you. The staff at the detention center will contact you about any follow-up procedures.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: And you'll have to complete that rigmarole yourself.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I understand.
Detention Center of the Foundation
Kakania stops at the iron gate of the detention center.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member II
items.text: Please fill out this visitor sheet, including your name, time of visit, and purpose.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You know, in many ways, the Foundation headquarters remind me of Vienna.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Especially in moments like this.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: All done. Here you are.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member II
items.text: Thanks for your cooperation. Please stand behind me. I'll open the door for you.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member II
items.text: You'll have to go inside alone. Remember, you have 30 minutes before the lights turn off. Once time's up, you need to come out as quickly as possible.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Thank you.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *exhale*

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: After three rounds of procedures to obtain approval for the visit and discussions with four departments to allow me to bring personal items, I'm finally here.
Her voice gets quieter and quieter as she speaks.
Because she hears familiar, ethereal singing.
Enthralled, she makes her way to its source.
It's Isolde. She's singing.
Not an aria, but the Tristan chord.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Can you still hear them?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: They are out of my hearing already

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Anxious fears confuse your ear

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: You are misled by the grove's whisperings

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Laughingly rustling in the wind

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The calling of horns does not sound so sweet

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It is the stream's gently murmuring waves

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Flowing along so gaily

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: How could I hear that if horns were still calling?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: In the still of the night

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: It is just stream that laughs with me

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: He who is waiting for me

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: In the silence of the night

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: *exhale*
She softly responds.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "That old tune ... Why does it waken me?"

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "Where am I?"

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "I cannot tell you."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "I was ..."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "... where I had been before,"

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "and where I am destined to go."
She stops, taking a table mirror out of her bag.
This table mirror has attended countless treatments, including Isolde's. Its cracks are clear to see.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This belongs to you, Isolde.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Goodbye.
The stand makes a noise as she puts the mirror on the marble floor, yet it doesn't wake the lucid dreamer.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Doctor.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Listen, the fallen leaves rustle when you step on them.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Isn't it just like a beautiful song?
There is no response but the sound of footsteps growing ever more distant. Footsteps that once echoed in the streets of Vienna, and will continue to echo in her dreams.
But not here.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You said you had a personal opinion on Isolde's condition.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: May I ask what your opinion is? Why is she behaving like this?

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: When a person experiences trauma that is too severe to bear, they will often revert to a time when they felt the safest and happiest.

items.speaker: Psychiatrist
items.text: So I assume that, in her mind, time has been frozen in the best days of her life.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: If you've made up your mind and think I'm guilty, why do you treat me so gently?

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: If this is the salvation you brought,

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: I will embrace it with joy.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: Look, Doctor.

items.speaker: Isolde
items.text: The stars are shining.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If you knew you were living in a dream made of lies, would you still embrace it?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If this is the salvation you'd hoped for,

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I will accept it. If I must.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Miss, you may close the door.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I've ended the visit early.

items.speaker: Foundation Staff Member II
items.text: But you left your mirror behind. It's against the—

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know, I know. I signed the agreement.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But it's in the corridor, not her room. Could you at least leave it there for a day and take it away tomorrow?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You can put it in my record as a member of the Field Agent Administration.
Ms. Kakania!
She turns toward the voice and finds a familiar figure standing by the other end of the gate.
It's Marcus.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ms. Marcus! I didn't expect to see you here!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I just returned from a field mission. I hurried over as soon as I heard you were here.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But did I just hear that correctly? Have you joined the Field Agent Administration?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: There must be other choices. You don't have to—

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes, there are. But I've already decided. I will join the Field Agent Administration.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I couldn't possibly work in government. That's never been my goal, and never will be.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I wanted to introduce you to the Timekeeper before you made a decision. She also leads an independent team.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But I've already made up my mind, Ms. Marcus.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Umm.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: D-Do you know what kind of institution the History Maintenance Team is?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I-I mean, its members and the missions they perform ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Yes, I'm fully aware. They're an expendable unit. Field agents can be abandoned at any time.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The name explains itself.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Would you give a second thought to meeting with the Timekeeper? Maybe after talking with her, you'll have another choice, and—

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I'd love to meet her! But only because she's a friend of yours.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Perhaps, after meeting this friend who can forecast the "Storm," I can finally bid farewell to our old era and welcome this new one.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I suppose your mind's made up, then ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We all have our responsibilities to bear, and this is mine.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Our era was so brutally washed away. You saw it, too. And with the History Maintenance Team, I can do something to prevent the destruction of others' eras.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's the right thing to do, don't you think?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Is this farewell?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I've already said goodbye once, so no, it isn't.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Though I cannot guarantee anything, there is a voice in my head that says:

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: "One day, I will see you again."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But this isn't the best place to chat. Let's go.
She points through the gate. Outside, the moon tenderly climbs up the sky.
She walks outside without looking back.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: After all, the path before us is the only way ahead.
